pages.text: A $(item)Phone PABX$() is the exchange every $(l:radiocraft:telephones/telephone)telephone$(/l) needs. Phones touching it or on its $(l:radiocraft:radios/data_wire)data wire$(/l) call each other by extension. It needs power from the power wire, and its phones draw through it, so a big system needs a stronger supply; its lamp is green while it has power.$(br2)Right click it to set it up: fill in the boxes and press Save.

pages.title: Settings
pages.text: $(li)$(thing)Master number$(): dialed before an extension to reach this PABX. Three digits, or none (then only its own phones can call it).$(li)$(thing)First extension$(): its phones are numbered from here, 100 by default. Changing it numbers them all again.$(li)$(thing)All-Call extension$(): rings all its phones; the first to answer takes the call.$(li)$(thing)PABX name$(): up to 10 letters, shown on a phone keying its master number.

pages.title: Calling other PABXes
pages.text: PABXes on one data wire, or across a $(l:radiocraft:microwave/microwave_radio)microwave link$(/l), reach each other. Dial the other PABX's master number, then the extension: master 603, extension 100 is $(thing)603100$(). An extension on your own PABX always wins.$(br2)A microwave radio alone is not an exchange: phones on it need a PABX too.

pages.title: Linked PABXes
pages.text: PABXes that reach each other and share a master number act as one: their phones dial each other by extension alone. A number can only be used once across them. If two phones have it, neither can be called and $(thing)EXT IN USE$() flashes until one changes.$(br2)An All-Call extension also rings a linked PABX's phones if that PABX has the same All-Call extension.
